description: The 'DUMMY' five-byte-prefix branch at app/cbl/COADM01C.cbl:138 and the statements it guards at 147-154, entered through the PADDED form of an option: a re-entry carrying CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1, an AID of DFHENTER and OPTIONI ' 1' - a space in byte 1, the digit in byte 2 - which is the mirror image of case07's '1 ' and the one input shape in this directory whose INSPECT has a space to replace on a VALID option. Line 87's IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is false, so the ELSE at 91 runs: RECEIVE-MENU-SCREEN, then the ordered three-way EVALUATE at 93-103, whose FIRST arm is DFHENTER and whose WHEN OTHER is last, so PROCESS-ENTER-KEY is what runs. The normalisation at 117-125 with every intermediate, and it DIVERGES from case07 at the very first step: (1) the descending scan at 117-121 starts at WS-IDX = LENGTH OF OPTIONI = 2 and tests before it varies, and byte 2 here is '1', which is NOT = SPACES, so the loop exits IMMEDIATELY with WS-IDX = 2 - where case07's and case03's '1 ' found byte 2 blank and had to walk down to 1, and case04's '  ' walked down to 1 and stopped only on the WS-IDX = 1 leg of the same condition; (2) line 122 sends OPTIONI(1:WS-IDX) - two characters this time, the whole field - into WS-OPTION-X, declared PIC X(02) JUST RIGHT at line 45, and because the sender already fills the receiver the right-justification is a no-op and the image stays ' 1'; (3) line 123's INSPECT REPLACING ALL ' ' BY '0' is what earns its keep here, turning the LEADING space into a zero and giving '01' - in case06's '05' and case09's '02' there is no space to replace at all, so this is the case where that statement is load-bearing on an option that goes on to be accepted; (4) line 124 moves it into WS-OPTION PIC 9(02), which is 1; (5) line 125 echoes WS-OPTION into OPTIONO as '01'. The padded and the unpadded route therefore converge on the same 1, which is exactly why this case pins the same normalised echo a case fed '1 ' would: the chain is proved by the intermediates it passes through, not by a different answer, and the two shapes together are the padded and unpadded input this normalisation has to survive. The map already agrees with the receiver - app/bms/COADM01.bms:145-149 declares OPTION with ATTRB=(FSET,IC,NORM,NUM,UNPROT) and JUSTIFY=(RIGHT,ZERO), so a real terminal would deliver the digit already right-justified and zero-filled - which makes the program's own normalisation belt and braces rather than the only line of defence; it is reproduced because the program performs it, not because it is needed. The guard at 127-129 is evaluated in source order and every term is false: WS-OPTION IS NOT NUMERIC is false, WS-OPTION > CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT is false because 1 is not greater than the one entry this case's table declares active - the INCLUSIVE upper boundary of its valid range, the same off-by-one that app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy:20's count of 4 draws at 4 and that case06's '05' sits immediately outside - and WS-OPTION = ZEROS is false. So no message is composed at 131-132, SEND-MENU-SCREEN is not performed from 133, and WS-ERR-FLG stays 'N'. Line 137's IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON therefore holds, and line 138 reference-modifies the first five characters of CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION): subscript 1, Java position 0, the one-based-to-zero-based conversion pinned here at the first element. app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy names no program beginning DUMMY - its four entries are COUSR00C, COUSR01C, COUSR02C and COUSR03C - so this branch cannot be reached from the copybook table at all, and it must still be exercised, because dead and unreachable code is preserved rather than cleaned up. The table handed in therefore differs from the copybook's first entry in NOTHING BUT THE PROGRAM NAME: same option number, same PIC X(35) name, so the program name is the only variable under test and the composed OPTN001O line below is byte-identical to the real one. The prefix is what line 138 tests, so the remaining three bytes are ordinary name characters and the injected name is a full PIC X(08). Because those five characters ARE 'DUMMY', the XCTL at 142-145 is skipped in its entirety and the three mutations at 139-141 never happen: CDEMO-FROM-TRANID is NOT set to 'CA00', CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is NOT set to 'COADM01C', CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is NOT zeroed, and all sixteen fields of the 160-byte area of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy come back exactly as they were supplied, CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT still 1 and so still a re-entry. Those three mutations are correct on the transfer path and wrong here, and the difference is the whole of what this expectation pins: a translation that mutated the communication area before testing the prefix would pass case07 and fail here. Echoing the remaining thirteen fields untouched is the assertion of statelessness - COADM01C reads no other context field and writes no other, and the state travels in the payload rather than in a session. Had the transfer run it would have carried COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) at 144, unlike the sign-on transfer at 165-167 which names only a program and passes no communication area at all; the two are not interchangeable, case07 pins the one that passes the area and case10 the one that does not, and this case pins the third possibility, that neither runs. Skipping the transfer is also what makes 147-154 reachable: they sit AFTER the inner END-IF on line 146, so on the transfer path an XCTL that never returns is the only thing keeping them out, and this is the ONLY path in the program that executes them. Line 147 blanks WS-MESSAGE, line 148 moves DFHGREEN over the COLOR=RED that app/bms/COADM01.bms:154-157 declares for ERRMSG - the only attribute byte COADM01C ever writes, and the reason the expected send carries ERRMSGC and nothing else - lines 149-153 STRING 'This option ' and 'is coming soon ...' into the message with NOTHING between them, because the CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-NAME operand at 150-151 is commented out in the source and stays commented out, and line 154 sends. Note what that message does not mean: WS-ERR-FLG is still 'N', so this is a SUCCESSFUL outcome that happens not to transfer, not a rejection. The green attribute in place of the map's red is the program saying so itself, and case04, case05, case06, case11, case18 and case20 are the rejections, every one of which keeps the red and sets the flag. The send at 154 goes through SEND-MENU-SCREEN, so POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at 174 and BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS at 175 both run and the response names map COADM1A of mapset COADM01, the same pair the RECEIVE at 191-197 used and the same pair the CSD binds to transaction CA00. BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS loops from 1 until WS-IDX exceeds CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT, which for this table is 1, so it composes OPTN001O and stops: lines 233-236 STRING the option number, '. ' and the PIC X(35) name into WS-ADMIN-OPT-TXT PIC X(40), giving '01' then '. ' then the thirty-five-character name, thirty-nine characters padded to forty. The other eleven lines are the point of the eleven LOW-VALUES images below. They are low values and not spaces because nothing wrote them: the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COADM1AO that clears the whole symbolic output area is at line 89 inside the ENTER branch ONLY and does not run on a re-entry, so those lines still hold what an initialised WORKING-STORAGE item with no VALUE clause holds, and BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS never reaches them. All eleven are pinned explicitly rather than left unstated, so the no-reset state is well defined rather than accidental - and pinned on the OUTPUT side rather than as re-supplied input fields because COADM1AO REDEFINES COADM1AI at app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY:139 and the two views share the same forty data bytes, so declaring them as spaces on the way in would contradict the low values asserted on the way out. Only OPTIONI is read. The message channel is the eighty-byte WS-MESSAGE of line 38 and not the seventy-eight of ERRMSGO: line 177 moves the one into the other and app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY:138 declares ERRMSGI PIC X(78), so two bytes are lost on the way to the screen - immaterial for a thirty-character message, and case11 pins the eighty while case15 pins the seventy-eight. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the timestamp COADM01C's own version footer carries, so the instant is anchored in the source rather than chosen; all twenty cases in this directory pin that same instant and name US-ASCII explicitly rather than leaving a code page to a platform default. This path does paint a header, so the pinned instant is what makes that paint reproducible rather than clock-dependent. Every expected value above is STATICALLY DERIVED - read out of the COBOL paragraph that produces it and cross-checked against the 160-byte layout of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, the option table of app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy, the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY and the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COADM01.bms - and NONE of it was captured from, recorded against or replayed from an execution of the legacy program, which is empirically impossible here: no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from the repository. ParityCase's own class documentation is the authoritative statement of that provenance, and the substitution of provenance - and of provenance alone, since the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand - is escalated for explicit confirmation rather than silently absorbed (risk R-A). HOW THE OPTION TABLE IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA: the branch at :138 reference-modifies CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-PGMNAME(1:5) and compares it against 'DUMMY', and app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy names no program beginning DUMMY - so no arrangement of the copybook table, and no seeded row of any dataset, can reach it. The OCCURS slots are storage rather than data. This case therefore declares unitStimulus.environment.MENU_TABLE_VARIANT = 'DUMMY_PREFIX_FIRST_ENTRY', which is the whole of the input the adapter needs to build a single-entry table differing from the copybook's first entry in NOTHING BUT THE PROGRAM NAME: the same option number 1 and the same PIC X(35) 'User List (Security)' name, so the program name is the only variable under test and the composed OPTN001O line stays byte-identical to the real one. It is declared here rather than chosen by an adapter that recognised the string 'case08', because an adapter keyed on a case identifier means this file gives no indication which table it runs over, and renumbering it would silently move the branch to a different case. An unrecognised variant is refused by the adapter rather than ignored, so a mistyped declaration fails loudly instead of quietly running the copybook table and reporting a clean diff for the wrong reason.
